title: MIT researchers develop CheMeleon machine-learning model
excerpt: The open-source foundation model uses molecular descriptors to predict chemical properties.
bodyHtml:
According to MIT News on November 6, 2026, researchers at MIT developed an open-source machine-learning model called CheMeleon to predict how chemical compounds behave. The findings were reported in the Sept. 14 issue of the Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling in a paper by Akshat Shirish Zalte, Jackson Burns, Charlles Abreu, William Green, and three researchers from the chemical company BASF.

The model was built using ChemProp, an open-source machine-learning package developed and maintained by the Green group at MIT. CheMeleon uses molecular descriptors of a million molecules from PubChem, a large, freely available database of chemical information maintained by the U.S. National Institutes of Health. The model is pre-trained to learn correlations between the structure of a given molecule and how it behaves with respect to a catalog of about 1,600 descriptors.

In a contest organized by OpenADMET for trying to predict the properties of a variety of new molecules that had not previously been synthesized, nine of the top 20 entries had used CheMeleon in their process. The work was supported by the Machine Learning for Pharmaceutical Discovery and Synthesis consortium, along with fellowship support from U.S. Department of Energy and MathWorks.
